facts.rejected_reason: issue #245's 'needs hand separator' slice: the CFN registry's primary_identifier=[CertificateAuthorityArn, Principal] is composite (len>1), but the provider's aws_acmpca_permission.html.markdown carries no Import section at all - no import block, no `terraform import` example, nothing. There is no worked example anywhere in the doc to read a separator character off, and inventing one (a comma, a colon) would be a guess dressed as evidence. A fuller extraction would need the provider to document an import path for this resource at all; until it does, the separator genuinely has no source. Left unadmitted.

CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (#242, wall/servermint): the sentence above is accurate about the import ID's shape and wrong about what that shape costs. A composite whose parent scope is config-supplied and whose remaining segment is server-minted is not outside this table's vocabulary - internal/live/identity/table_generated.go carries 51 ServerAssigned rows with a separator in their ImportSyntax, and ImportSyntax is documentation only (TypeIdentity's own doc comment): a ServerAssigned row never builds its identity from Components, it reads it back from discovery. The actual blocker is SERVER-ASSIGNED IDENTITY WITH NO MARKER-CAPABLE ARGUMENT, BLOCKED ON #233. live/survey-full.json records signals.taggable=false for this type at v6.59.0, so admitting it would put every instance in NeedsDiscovery, make stamp.go:743's mustStamp true, and raise an unconditional unstampable fatal at stamp.go:537 - and live-mv's locateByList (mv.go:673) would match on a tofu-address tag that cannot exist, reporting "No live resource carries estate X and address Y" about an account it never checked. That is strictly worse than today's refusal, which is why this stays. EVIDENCE FOR THE SHAPE, recomputed from committed artifacts rather than quoted: the provider's v6.59.0 identity schema requires id, rest_api_id for import, of which id has no Argument Reference bullet at any block depth in the pinned doc cache. The four taggable members of the same bucket (aws_ecs_task_set, aws_eks_pod_identity_association, aws_prometheus_anomaly_detector, aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace) were admitted in the same batch, because for them the ownership marker is the discriminator and the parent scope only narrows the candidate set: parent-scoped enumeration can CONFIRM an identity the configuration has already narrowed to one, it cannot SUPPLY one.

REASON RECORDED 2026-08-19 (#309); the entry carried none before, only its recovered_from provenance. This type is untaggable (live/survey-full.json signals.taggable=false at v6.59.0, and the schema carries no tags attribute) and AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient's primary_identifier is [UserPoolId, ClientId] of which only ClientId is in read_only_properties - a server-minted leaf under a config-known parent. That PARTIAL read-only shape is why the type is neither admitted nor vetoed: tools/row-gen/markerless.go consults classify.go's bucketServerAssigned, which requires the primary identifier be WHOLLY read-only, and sourcesAgree is false because ClientId is read-only, so markerless() falls through to '!classifiedServerAssigned && !docServerMinted' and returns false. The type therefore never enters internal/live/identity.MarkerlessTypes, and identity.LocatedType's first condition is membership in that set - so issue #270's record-located path, which is the mechanism this shape actually needs, never evaluates it. Admitting it as a plain ServerAssigned row instead is closed for the reason aws_cognito_managed_login_branding's entry gives and which was re-verified in code on 2026-08-19: every instance lands in NeedsDiscovery, stamp.go:940's mustStamp is true (the block's DiscoveryCause does not BindsByName), and stamp raises the unstampable error. The unique-name rescue (uniquename.go, #272) is the only mechanism that admits an untaggable ServerAssigned type today - it is what admits all four of them (aws_cloudfront_cache_policy, aws_cloudfront_origin_request_policy, aws_cloudfront_response_headers_policy, aws_route53_cidr_collection) - and it does not reach this type: the registry entry carries no unique_name_property, correctly, because Cognito does not document ClientName as unique within a pool. TWO FURTHER PREREQUISITES, both measured rather than argued: (a) identity.credentialMaterial fires on this schema - client_secret is Sensitive and not Deprecated at v6.59.0 - so LocatedType's second condition refuses it even once the first is met; (b) LocatedType's third condition assumes the top-level string 'id' IS the import identity ('the attribute OpenTofu's own import path round-trips'), and that premise is false for this type: the provider's own Attribute Reference says 'id - ID of the user pool client' while the Import section's example is 'us-west-2_abc123/3ho4ek12345678909nh3fmhpko', i.e. <user_pool_id>/<client_id>. writeBackLocated records obj.id and materializeLocated imports that string, so a located admission as the mechanism stands today would record the leaf and fail at the next import. POPULATION, computed at bdcc47a6b8 from live/survey-full.json + live/mapping.json + live/registry.json + live/import-grammar.json + hashicorp/aws 6.59.0 schemas: 18 types are untaggable, unadmitted, unvetoed, mapped, and carry a PARTIALLY read-only primary identifier (12 of them API Gateway v1/v2); 16 of the 18 have a composite documented import (separator non-null) and so hit prerequisite (b); 1 (this one) hits (a); exactly 2 (aws_elastic_beanstalk_configuration_template, aws_vpn_gateway_attachment) would work under the located mechanism as it stands. Widening the markerless veto to the partial shape must therefore NOT land before the located payload can carry a composite identity, or 16 types move from an honest refusal to a deferred import failure. RESOLVED 2026-08-19 through 2026-08-23 (#309 step 2 commit 5444949ceb, #329 commit 250fd46952, #337 commit 4e8aa97313, ruling 5 commit 2019d8dd73), then re-verified 2026-08-28 (#429): every prerequisite this entry named has cleared, in the order it demanded. #329/#337 landed the composite located payload FIRST - LocatedIdentityPlanFor now returns a Composite (provider identity object), Composed (documented import-ID string, issue #337's DocumentedImportIDs) or Named plan alongside the original bare-id default, and LocatedRecordFrom/materializeLocated write and read all four shapes, not obj.id unconditionally. #309 step 2 THEN widened markerless.go's veto to the partial-read-only shape (5444949ceb): this type is in MarkerlessTypes today. Prerequisite (a) cleared separately: ruling 5 (2019d8dd73) replaced LocatedType's whole-schema credentialMaterial veto with sensitiveIdentityAttr, which asks only whether the RECORDED attributes are sensitive - client_secret is not one of them (this type's plan reads user_pool_id and id) - so the credential wall no longer fires. Prerequisite (b) cleared by #337's docimportid_generated.go grammar (Separator '/', Parts userpoolid/id) plus this type's own membership in IDNotProvenWholeTypes, which routes LocatedIdentityPlanFor to the Composed branch instead of trusting the bare leaf. CHOUDOUFU_LIVE_SCHEMAS=1's TestLocatedTypePopulation (internal/live/identity/located_test.go), run fresh against hashicorp/aws 6.59.0 on 2026-08-28, places this type in that test's 'composed' bucket, not 'credential' or any refusal bucket: it is LocatedType-admitted today. The write leg is pinned by value in internal/live/liveimport/located_admission_test.go (TestRatifyAdmitsAMarkerlessNoRatifiedRowTypeThroughLocatedType, recorded ImportID 'us-west-2_abc123/3ho4ek12345678909nh3fmhpko'); the read/import leg - materializeLocated importing that exact string rather than an identity object or the bare leaf - is pinned by internal/live/projection/located_composed_test.go's TestComposedLocatedRoundTripImportsTheDocumentedString (#429), mutation-checked against the pre-#329/#337 obj.id-only behavior. The POPULATION line above is UNCHANGED as history (it is what bdcc47a6b8 measured) but is no longer live: MarkerlessTypes grew from 140 to 158+ types after #309 step 2, so 'the 18-type population' is a strict subset of a much larger admitted set today, not a live refusal count. Of the two flat-case names in that line, only aws_vpn_gateway_attachment still 'works under the located mechanism as it stands' (pinned by internal/live/identity/located_flatregression_test.go); aws_elastic_beanstalk_configuration_template is now vetoed by NotImportableTypes (issue #331, unrelated to composite identity and landed after bdcc47a6b8) - a correct, safer refusal per HANDOFF's safety rule, not a defect. This entry stays in rejected.json because the underlying ruling it records - this type does not get a hand-ratified TABLE ROW (a Components-based identity resolved from configuration alone) - is still correct: ClientId is server-minted and cannot be resolved from configuration, which is exactly why the record-located route, not a table row, is the right mechanism for it. TestRejectedLedgerIsDisjointFromAdmitted only checks disjointness against identity.AdmittedTypes() (DefaultTable's ratified rows), which this type has never joined and does not join here.
